chunks: All praise is due to Allah, the First before every first, and the Last after every last,
His Firstness necessitates that there is no first before Him, and His Lastness necessitates that there is no last after Him,
and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, a testimony in which the secret matches the open declaration, and the heart matches the tongue.

key_terms.الْآخِرِ: The Last, one of the Divine Names
key_terms.الْأَوَّلِ: The First, one of the Divine Names (Asma ul-Husna)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for Allah to be the First and the Last in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In the context of the 'Vicissitudes of Time' (Tahawwulat al-Azminah), Imam Ali uses this supplication to anchor the believer's consciousness in Allah's transcendence beyond temporal change, establishing Him as the immutable reference point for all creation. The requirement that the 'secret' (inner state) matches the 'public' (utterance) reflects the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) as the essence of true worship, ensuring that theological affirmation translates into spiritual reality.

en.sayed-ali-raza: He (Allāh) is the First before every first and the Last after every last.
His Firstness necessitates that there is no (other) first before Him and His Lastness necessitates that there is no other last after Him.
I do stand witness that there is no god but Allah both openly as well as secretly, with heart as well as with tongue.
